english_verification.review_scope: Translated the complete source article body before its National Ideas appendix and all 38 non-national-ideas pointers. Read representative current-Mod history, branch, and second-phase mission passages, plus the relevant paragraphs in all three cited English Wiki chunks; no exhaustive mission audit or runtime test. The primary compared native idea names/descriptions with current English localisation keys (formatting codes stripped); B32 upgraded Farranean originals also use their separate flavour file. Wide source bounds are locator envelopes, not exhaustive line-by-line audits. No formal validators, tests, builds or browser checks were run.
unresolved: The Istralore country page spells the founder Istralara, while the Warsinger page and local text use Istralania; prose follows the latter and the difference remains documented.
The Wiki supplies setting history, not authority on current mission ownership or implementation; local Mod scripts control those claims.
The branch is verified in local scripts, but the complete post-formation A58 mission tree and runtime outcomes were not exhaustively audited or playtested.
Community campaign difficulty evidence includes a Very Easy run and is not generalized to standard difficulty.

rationale.campaign_length: The 38 direct missions span two phases, with an optional branch to form Dameria.
rationale.colonization: Overseas colonization is not central; the Sarhal objectives focus on naval expeditions and religious expansion.
rationale.complexity: War, imperial diplomacy, parliament, religion, and branching missions are tightly interwoven.
rationale.dark_story: Revenge and religious coercion appear, but this is not a horror or extermination campaign.
rationale.difficulty: The country has a stable base; the main challenge comes from imperial politics and mission pacing, not a weak start.
rationale.diplomacy: Elector votes, the throne, old Moon Party alliances, and accession objectives demand sustained diplomatic work.
rationale.early_pressure: Survival pressure is limited, but expansion within the Empire quickly builds aggressive expansion and unlawful-territory problems.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: Magic and artificery are not everyday core loops.
rationale.narrative_density: The Lilac Wars’ legacy, dynastic succession, religious conversion, and identity choice form a continuous story.
rationale.tall_play: Military industry, ports, and prosperity projects are present, but chiefly serve imperial expansion.
rationale.trade_economy: Development around Dameria’s capital and its ports provides economic objectives, not a separate core mechanic.
rationale.warfare: The Banshees, officer education, Imperial Wars, and the Fifth Lilac War keep military affairs central throughout.

identity.appearance: An elector at the 1444 start; at the campaign midpoint it can form Dameria (A58) or retain A45 and unlock its dedicated second-phase missions.

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas and ambition only; optional idea groups and racial/government bonuses are excluded. Conditional alternatives are separate, not stacked. Accepting new ideas on formation depends on the actual event/decision and player choice.

description.text: With the end of the Wars of Rule in the late 13th century came Istralore’s ascension as Marshal of the Imperial Army and Elector of the Empire. Despite holding such a powerful position, its dukes and duchesses have (almost) never attempted to further their own interests and have instead sternly held fast to their duties.
description.text_en: With the end of the Wars of Rule in the late 13th century came Istralore’s ascension as Marshal of the Imperial Army and Elector of the Empire. Despite holding such a powerful position, its dukes and duchesses have (almost) never attempted to further their own interests and have instead sternly held fast to their duties.

description.text:
“My son, my blood, my joy, I speak not as your mother but as your Duchess. The world is unjust. Our true liege lies dead, murdered by a traitor. A traitor who sits upon the Dove Throne even now.

Even though we fought for what was right, Istralore lost both the battle and the war. I’ve failed my charge in too many ways to count. But, my fight isn’t over. Not til my last breath. Wex must be chastened. Lothane brought to account. Dameria avenged.

This is the duty and burden of Istralore. It is mine to bear. And when I’m gone it will be yours. Do you understand?”

“Yes, mothe- Duchess.”

- Duchess Aucanna I to the future Duke Aucan III

description.text:
Istralania Warsinger, founder and namesake of Istralore, was once known simply as Istralania ta Estadh. Usually a reserved and stoic woman, upon the battlefield, Istralania’s blood-curdling cries struck awe and terror in the minions of the Sorcerer-King Nichmer as she slew them by the hundreds. Over the course of the war, others would echo the elf’s battle cries, becoming her “banshees” and striking fear through the Black Legions of Castanor.

In the aftermath of war, Istralania’s Banshees formalized into an elite all-women unit. Forming the core of the Istralari army, the unit saw service through the century long Lilac Wars, Corinite Wars, Camir’s Conquest, and beyond.

description.text:
“Damnable fools, those Istralorians are. They’d rather plunge the entire Empire into war for the usurper Corin than heed their Emperor!“ - Emperor Galien I síl na Trisfer

With the revelation of Castellos’ death, the Regent Court began its plunge into chaos and final fragmentation. As the question of which god would succeed Castellos echoed through Cannor, a resounding response sounded out from Istralore - the Goddess of War Corin. Boldly defying the eleventh and final Pantheonic Council, the adoption of the Corinite faith solidified Istralore’s place as the frontline of future Corinite Accord within Anbennar.

description.text: Almost every Istralani noble can trace their lineage back to an elf aboard the Migrant Ship Estádha. Captained by Istralania Warsinger, she and the ship’s inhabitants were the first to accept Munas Moonsinger's bold claims and follow the moon towards a new home. Their show of courage convinced the rest of the Remnant Fleet to follow Munas as well, bringing an end to the thousand-year Great Wander. Today, centuries later, just as the blood of the Estádha still courses within Istralore, so too does that same courage and conviction to chart a course into the unknown.

description.text: Across the rolling hills of the Damerian Dales, the forested landscape is dotted by mines churning out ores of all sorts. But, this was not always so. At first, simple holes were dug by the ancient Damerid tribes to acquire the easiest deposits. Armed with iron might, these humble tribes rose to found the Damerian Republic, marking the start of a storied history. In the centuries after, as the Republic became Kingdom and later Grand Duchy, true mines sprung into being giving name to the Dalemines. With the final fall of Dameria, Istralore now stands as heir to the mines and its legacy.

description.text:
The First Great Damesear Raid was a disaster that stopped just shy of catastrophe. The Damish Temple of Moon Isle had been defiled by the demon worshipping gnolls of Viakkoc. Anbenncóst smoldered in the embers of demonflame. Thousands were dead, thousands more taken as slaves.

It was in this backdrop that Ricain Silistra, adventurer and future Duke of Istralore, rode across the countryside. Still covered with soot, sweat, and blood from fending off raiders, he swept from town to town waving the banner of Istralore’s venerable Sealion and calling upon every righteous soul to follow him. By the time of his arrival in Duchy’s capital of Cilseinn, thousands stood behind him. Planting the now tattered banner behind him, he proclaimed a new crusade -- in Corin’s name.

player_overview.avoid_if: It is a poor fit if you dislike HRE-style diplomacy, aggressive expansion and unlawful-territory pressure, or event-paced objectives instead of quiet development.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Rebuild the Moon Party through diplomacy and limited wars early on; make an identity and religious transition mid-campaign; then unify the Empire as emperor and expand toward Lorent and Sarhal.
player_overview.overview: You are a half-elf elector who, after the Lilac Wars, still refuses to recognize Wex’s usurpation. First reunite old Moon Party allies, reclaim Dameria’s homeland, and revive the elite female Banshees. At mid-campaign, either restore Dameria or retain Istralore and continue contesting the throne, unifying the Empire, and spreading Corinite faith. The cost is managing imperial expansion, elector diplomacy, and religious war at the same time.
player_overview.recommended_for: For players who enjoy restoration stories, imperial politics, elector diplomacy, women’s military traditions, Corinite religious wars, and major expansion in the middle and late game.
signature_features: Choose between restoring Dameria and retaining Istralore—a genuine identity choice that changes the campaign’s second half.
Revive the Banshees and use parliament to turn women’s military service, officer education, and labor rights into state reforms.
Contest the throne as elector and Imperial Marshal, then use Imperial Wars to reunite old allies and lost lands.
player_overview.tagline: Be the last Damerian loyalist who refuses to yield; then decide whether to restore the old moon or make Istralore the Empire’s new one.

reasons: 38 direct missions make a complete restoration story from the Lilac Wars’ defeat to imperial unification.
Restoring Dameria or retaining A45 changes the later missions and national story.
The Banshees and parliamentary reforms for women combine military development with social change in one main arc.
Elector diplomacy, competition for the throne, and Imperial Wars make expansion more than ordinary claim-based conquest.
The official Final Empire rework closely integrates Istralore with the revised imperial system.
warnings: Expansion inside the Empire simultaneously creates aggressive-expansion, unlawful-territory, and elector-relations pressure.
Missions often require diplomacy, espionage, parliamentary actions, and war objectives to progress in parallel.
Only retaining A45 unlocks the distinctive second phase; forming A58 switches to another country’s content.

positive_indicators: Access to labor and military service
values.rationale: Women’s education, labor rights, military service, and officer opportunities are explicit institutional positives. Restoration wars, religious unification, and imperial expansion chiefly affect expansion and restraint; they do not automatically erase the value of these reforms.
